In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of protein quality control in the endoplasmatic reticulum.
the identification and characterization of molecular chaperones of the endoplamic reticulum and the cytosol that are involved in protein folding and degradation of misfolded and aggregated proteins.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chaperones are essential for the proper folding of proteins in the endoplasmatic reticulum.

chaperone assisted retro-translocation of misfolded ER-resident proteins to the cytoplasm and subsequent degradation by the proteasome is a highly regulated, multi-step process, which is essential for the maintenance of the endoplasic reticulum homeostasis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality control machinery is a complex system with many different components that have to work together.
endoplasmic-reticulum associated protein quality control is a chaperone driven process.
the endoplasmatic reticulum is the place to be for misfolded proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chaperones of the endoplarmic reticulum have a dual function.
chaperone function is not limited to protein folding, but is also involved in protein unfolding, protein translocation and protein degradation.
the endoplasmatic reticulum contains a plethora of chaperone activity and that chaperone activity is not limited to the lumen of this organelle, but also occurs in the membrane.
